answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing correlation. Each identity posts a bond, and at every epoch's dawn the node tests random pairs for shared faults: same hosts, same timing, near-identical answers. Identities that fail together, clones drinking from one lagoon of infrastructure, are slashed jointly, scaled by cluster size squared, so splitting one stake across 50 heads multiplies the penalty instead of diluting it. An honest solo agent's bond stays basalt-solid, because its errors correlate with no one.
